subject.title: Bug: Billing error (402) causes infinite retry death spiral for inline-apiKey providers (no backoff)

question: Should OpenClaw adopt provider-level fail-closed cooldown state for inline `models.providers.<id>.apiKey` credentials, or keep cooldowns limited to auth profiles and document migration to profiles as the supported path?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the durable inline-key usage namespace and fail-closed upgrade behavior are auth-provider policy choices with compatibility impact.

options.title: Accept provider-level cooldown
options.body: Land or rebuild the linked fix so inline keys get the same billing/auth cooldown protection as profile-backed credentials.

options.title: Keep profile-only cooldowns
options.body: Treat auth profiles as the supported cooldown boundary and document moving inline keys into profiles as the workaround instead of changing runtime behavior.

options.title: Request narrower design
options.body: Pause the linked PR until maintainers specify the exact cooldown identity, persistence, and recovery behavior they want.

recommendation.title: Accept provider-level cooldown
recommendation.body: Land or rebuild the linked fix so inline keys get the same billing/auth cooldown protection as profile-backed credentials.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest maintainer-side routing candidate in the observed auth/provider history and issue timeline for this product-direction choice.
